against: another person with their own account on this machine reading them
a service in the stack reading a credential meant for a different service, since each is handed only what it authenticates with
them appearing in a support bundle, a diagnosis, a log line or an error message, which are filtered on the way out
not_against: anything running as you, which includes any program you install and any malware that reaches your account
an unencrypted backup or a copy taken off this machine — a backup is exactly as sensitive as the credentials in it
an administrator of this machine, who can read any file on it
anyone who reads the disk while it is unlocked, or an unencrypted disk taken out of the machine
protection.summary: Credentials are stored as text in files owned by you. They are not encrypted: anything that can read the file can read the credential.
